description: "We are a team of mechanical engineering and science students, new to hackathons and eager to learn. We bring strengths in mechanical design, science and problem-solving. We're looking for teammates with Python or data analysis skills. Beginners welcome!"
summary: MECH ORBIT is a zero-setup, browser-based SPHEREx Sky Explorer designed to democratize access to NASA’s infrared astronomy data. Official archives like the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) hold massive datasets, but querying coordinates and handling FITS files requires advanced Python or SQL coding skills. MECH ORBIT eliminates this technical barrier through an interactive Streamlit web application that connects directly to NASA IRSA. Students, educators, and citizen scientists can enter sky coordinates and a search radius to query real SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 observations in seconds. Users can inspect clean metadata tables, download results as CSV files, and visualize or compare FITS images side-by-side without installing specialized desktop software. By turning raw infrared space archives into an accessible, mobile- and desktop-friendly tool, MECH ORBIT accelerates scientific curiosity and empowers everyday learners to explore real NASA mission data.
details: What it does & How it works: MECH ORBIT is a web-based astronomical exploration platform built with Python and Streamlit that connects directly to the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA). Users simply input sky coordinates and a search radius in the sidebar to query public SPHEREx mission collections (DR1 and QR3) in real time, retrieving thousands of matching infrared records within seconds.Key Features & Benefits:• No-Code Sky Search: Removes the need for complex SQL queries or heavy desktop software. • Metadata & One-Click CSV Export: Displays structured observation records in clean tables that can be downloaded instantly for offline study. • FITS Image Explorer & Comparison: Renders FITS images directly in the browser and allows side-by-side comparison of two observations. • Smart Error Handling: Uses automated retry logic and clear fallback alerts when direct FITS image URLs are unavailable, ensuring users still get complete metadata. Tools & Technologies Used:• Frontend & UI: Python, Streamlit (responsive for both mobile and desktop) • Data Processing: Astropy, Pandas (for coordinate handling, FITS parsing, and CSV generation) • Data Source: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) – SPHEREx DR1 & QR3 datasets Creativity & Impact: By separating FITS image resolution from tabular metadata, the platform prevents dead ends for beginners. It transforms complex space mission archives into an intuitive classroom and self-study tool for students and citizen scientists.
